Access to Conjugated Dienes and Cyclic Allenes via a Diazo-Dithiane
Rearrangement Cascade
Zhuzhu Zhang, Xiaomeng Gong, Yingze Jin, Rui-Peng Li,* and Shouchu Tang*
ACCESS
ABSTRACT: A transition-metal-free, base-promoted cascade between alkynyl-1,3-dithianes and α-diazodiesters has been
developed. The reaction proceeds through an anion relay chemistry (ARC) featuring a selective 1,3-sulfur rearrangement, enabling
divergent access to eight-membered sulfur-containing conjugated dienes and cyclic allenes in a one-pot fashion. This transformation
unveils new diazo reactivity beyond classical carbene pathways and highlights the synthetic utility of sulfur-based anionic processes.
S
ulfur-containing heterocycles are ubiquitous structural
motifs in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, natural products,
and functional materials.<sup>1</sup> While small sulfur heterocycles such
as thiophenes are well established synthetically,<sup>2</sup> the
preparation of medium-sized (8−10-membered) sulfur rings
remains a formidable challenge owing to transannular strain
and conformational rigidity.<sup>3,4</sup> Despite their unique electronic
and three-dimensional features, such scafolds are rarely
explored in drug discovery due to the lack of eficient synthetic
methods.<sup>5</sup> Therefore, developing general and eficient
strategies to access medium-sized sulfur heterocycles under
mild conditions is of considerable importance in synthetic and
medicinal chemistry.
To date, several strategies have been developed for the
construction of medium-sized sulfur-containing heterocycles,
including intramolecular transition-metal-catalyzed cyclization,
radical-mediated processes, and ring-expansion reactions
(Scheme 1a).<sup>6</sup> Among sulfur-rich building blocks, 1,3-dithianes
are particularly attractive due to their stability and versatile
reactivity beyond their traditional role as carbonyl protecting
groups.<sup>7</sup> Early work by Oku demonstrated ring expansion of
thioacetals via sulfonium ylide intermediates,<sup>6b</sup>
and Terada
later achieved an enantioselective variant using chiral
phosphoric acid (CPA) catalysis.<sup>6f</sup> Among medium-sized
sulfur heterocycles, cyclic allenes and conjugated dienes have
attracted particular interest due to their structural uniqueness
and potential applications. While significant progress has been
made, methods for their general and selective synthesis remain
limited. Wang and co-workers reported an Au-catalyzed
rearrangement of propargylic 1,3-dithianes to cyclic allenes,
with conjugated dienes formed only when specific substituents
were present at the 2-position of the dithiane ring
.<sup>8a</sup> Similarly,
Yucel described a base-mediated rearrangement of 1,3-
dithianyl-substituted propargylamines, delivering nine-mem-
bered sulfur-containing heterocycles bearing an internal
conjugated diene motif under mild conditions.<sup>8b</sup> Although
these studies represent elegant contributions, existing strategies
remain largely metal-catalyzed and are often limited to specific
substrate types. Consequently, the development of transition-
metal-free approaches that provide broader synthetic flexibility
remains highly desirable.
Diazo compounds have been extensively studied; however,
transition-metal-free couplings between diazo species and
heteroatom-stabilized carbanions remain underexplored.<sup>9</sup>
Metal-free diazo transformations are synthetically appealing
because they circumvent potential metal contamination and
often proceed under milder conditions. Building on our
previous studies of base-promoted anion relay chemistry
(ARC) and 1,3-sulfur rearrangements,<sup>10</sup> we envisioned that
the nucleophilic anion generated from alkynyl-1,3-dithianes
could undergo a carbene-free anionic coupling with α-
diazodiesters, followed by a 1,3-sulfur rearrangement to furnish

and Terada

attracted particular interest due to their structural uniqueness

these studies represent elegant contributions, existing strategies
remain largely metal-catalyzed and are often limited to specific
substrate types. Consequently, the development of transition-
metal-free approaches that provide broader synthetic flexibility
remains highly desirable.

Using alkynyl-1,3-dithiane 1a and α-diazodiester 2a as
model substrates (Table 1), we identified KO<sup>t</sup>Bu (1.5 equiv) as
the optimal base in DMSO at room temperature, afording the
conjugated diene 3a in 88% yield (Entry 1). Control
experiments confirmed the essential role of base and solvent:
no conversion was observed without base (Entry 2), weaker
bases such as NaO<sup>t</sup>Bu reduced the yield (39%) (Entry 3),
while DBU and
{ \mathrm { C s } } _ { 2 } { \mathrm { C O } } _ { 3 }
were inefective (Entries 4 and 5).
Among solvents, only DMSO enabled efective conversion;
THF completely suppressed reactivity, and DMF led to a
moderate yield of 65% (Entries 6 and 7). This unique DMSO
efect can be attributed to its ability to generate a nucleophilic
DMSO-derived carbanion under basic conditions, thereby
initiating the anionic relay, whereas other aprotic solvents fail
to provide such activation. Elevated temperature
( 6 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } )
led
to decomposition, emphasizing the importance of maintaining
mild conditions for this anionic cascade (Entry 8).
With optimized conditions, a wide range of aryl-substituted
alkynyl-1,3-dithianes underwent smooth transformation to
conjugated dienes
\mathbf { 3 a - 3 g }
in 75−88% yield (Scheme 2).
Electron-donating, electron-withdrawing, and sterically hin-
dered substituents were all well-tolerated. Extended aromatic
systems (benzofuranyl, piperonyl, naphthyl) also participated
smoothly (3h−3j, 77−81%). In contrast, alkyl-substituted
dithianes failed to produce detectable product 3k, under-
scoring the stabilizing role of aryl substituents in the
intermediate anions. Diverse α-diazodiesters were also
compatible, furnishing products 3l−3s in 80−87% yield. The
structure of 3l was unambiguously confirmed by X-ray
crystallography (CCDC 2427670).
Remarkably, the reaction outcome could be significantly
modulated by the choice of quenching reagent. Replacement of
_ { \mathrm { H } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O } }
with electrophilic alkyl halides (e.g., methyl iodide, benzyl
bromide, ethyl bromoacetate, 1-iodononane, and iodocyclo-
pentane) led to sulfur-containing cyclic allenes 4a−4i in 71−
86% yield (Scheme 3). This switchable reactivity underscores
the tunability of the anionic relay pathway and ofers a concise,
operationally simple approach to cyclic allene frameworks,
which serve as valuable intermediates for complex molecule
synthesis.

In summary, we have developed a transition-metal-free,
anion-relay cascade reaction between alkynyl-1,3-dithianes and
α-diazodiesters that enables the divergent synthesis of
conjugated dienes and cyclic allenes. This transformation
features a distinctive 1,3-sulfur rearrangement under mild basic
conditions, exhibits broad substrate scope with tunable
selectivity controlled by the electrophilic quencher, and
proceeds with operational simplicity and scalability. Impor-
tantly, this work expands diazo chemistry beyond conventional
carbene reactivity into the realm of anionic processes,
demonstrating the potential of sulfur-based anionic cascades
for the eficient construction of medium-sized heterocycles and
ofering a new conceptual framework for transition-metal-free
diazo coupling chemistry.
